source.author: verg
source.text: Me vero primum dulces ante omnia Musae, quarum sacra fero ingenti percussus amore, accipiant caelique vias et sidera monstrent, defectus solis varios lunaeque labores; unde tremor terris, qua vi maria alta tumescant obicibus ruptis rursusque in se ipsa residant, quid tantum Oceano properent se tinguere soles hiberni, vel quae tardis mora noctibus obstet.
source.text_original: Me vero primum dulces ante omnia Musae, / quarum sacra fero ingenti percussus amore, / accipiant caelique vias et sidera monstrent, / defectus solis varios lunaeque labores; / unde tremor terris, qua vi maria alta tumescant / obicibus ruptis rursusque in se ipsa residant, / quid tantum Oceano properent se tinguere soles / hiberni, vel quae tardis mora noctibus obstet.
source.text_english: But may the sweet Muses first of all receive me, whose holy rites I bear, struck with great love, and may they show the ways of heaven and the stars, the varying eclipses of the sun and the moon’s labors; whence comes the trembling on earth, by what force the deep seas swell when their barriers are broken and sink back again into themselves, why the winter suns hurry so much to dip themselves in Ocean, or what delay stands in the way of the slow nights.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Miror quomodo oblitus sis illos versiculos ponere: Unde tremor terris, qua vi maria alta tumescant, Obicibus ruptis, rursusque in seipsa residant: Defectus Solis varios, Lunaeque labores; Unde hominum genus, et pecudum: unde imber et ignes, Arcturum, pluviasque hyadas, geminosque Triones.
reuse.text_original: Miror quomodo oblitus sis illos versiculos ponere: Unde tremor terris, qua vi maria alta tumescant, Obicibus ruptis, rursusque in seipsa residant: Defectus Solis varios, Lunaeque labores; Unde hominum genus, et pecudum: unde imber et ignes, Arcturum, pluviasque hyadas, geminosque Triones.
reuse.text_english: I wonder how you could have forgotten to include those little verses: From where comes the trembling of the earth, by what force the deep seas swell, when their barriers are broken, and then settle back into themselves again; the varying eclipses of the Sun, and the troubles of the Moon; from where the race of men and of beasts; from where rain and fires, Arcturus and the rainy Hyades and the twin Bears.
